content.value_statement: Custom email domains require accurate DNS records and verified mail readiness. This skill guides Cooper Email setup, verification, inbox creation, and confirmed domain removal.
actual_capabilities: Guide domain addition with cooper_add_domain and a client_id for safe retries.
Explain returned MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, bounce, and verification records.
Distinguish automatic DNS updates from records the user must publish.
Diagnose missing or invalid DNS records using verification results and domain status.
Guide inbox creation after domain verification and receiving readiness.
Describe domain removal through the HTTP API with explicit user confirmation.
limitations: This skill provides instructions; actual operations require access to Cooper tools or the HTTP API.
It does not register domains or create DNS zones.
Users must publish DNS records unless the hostname is already a zone in Cooper's Cloudflare account.
Custom domains require an eligible plan, and DNS verification does not guarantee immediate receiving readiness.

use_cases.title: Launch branded agent inboxes
use_cases.description: Add a controlled subdomain, publish the returned DNS records, and create inboxes after verification.

use_cases.title: Diagnose domain verification failures
use_cases.description: Compare required records with reported DNS results and identify missing or invalid entries.

use_cases.title: Retire an email domain
use_cases.description: Review the documented removal behavior and confirm the target domain before using the HTTP deletion endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Understand setup requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the prerequisites for using agents.example.com with Cooper Email. Do not make changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a first custom domain

prompt_templates.title: Add a controlled subdomain
prompt_templates.prompt: I control agents.example.com and authorize adding it to Cooper Email. Check plan eligibility, use a client_id, and report returned DNS records.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my Cooper domain [domain_id]. Explain missing or invalid DNS records, respect verification rate limits, and report mail readiness without assuming success.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate inbox provisioning
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan inbox provisioning for [domain]. Prefer domain.verified events when available, otherwise respect verification rate limits. Create [username] only after verification and receiving readiness.

output_examples.input: What should I check before moving agent mail to my own domain?
output: Use a subdomain you control unless you explicitly want the root domain.
MX changes route all mail for the selected hostname.
Check your current Cooper plan for custom domain eligibility.
Publish the exact records returned when adding the domain.

output_examples.input: My verification response marks the verification TXT record missing. Can I create an inbox?
output: The reported verification TXT record is missing.
Publish the exact record returned by Cooper at your DNS provider.
Wait at least 60 seconds between manual verification checks.
Create the inbox only after domain verification and receiving readiness are confirmed.

output_examples.input: Explain domain removal before I authorize it.
output: Removal uses the domain deletion endpoint over HTTP.
The documented behavior restores the previous catch-all and deletes only DNS records Cooper created.
Confirm the domain identifier and your approval before proceeding.

best_practices: Use a controlled subdomain to limit MX routing changes to the intended email hostname.
Publish exact returned DNS values and confirm verification plus receiving readiness before creating inboxes.
Use client_id for safe retries and require explicit confirmation before domain removal.
anti_patterns: Changing root-domain MX records without explicit approval and awareness of existing mail routing.
Claiming verification succeeded without a confirming tool response.
Repeatedly triggering verification within 60 seconds or ignoring Retry-After responses.

faq.question: Which plans include custom domains?
faq.answer: The skill lists Free with zero, Starter with 15, and Pro with 200 custom domains. Check current billing status before adding one.

faq.question: Can this skill register a domain for me?
faq.answer: No. Cooper does not register domains or create DNS zones. Use a domain or subdomain you already control.

faq.question: Will Cooper publish my DNS records automatically?
faq.answer: Only when the hostname is already a zone in Cooper's Cloudflare account. Otherwise, publish the returned records at your DNS provider.

faq.question: How often can I verify a domain?
faq.answer: Manual verification is limited to once per 60 seconds. Respect HTTP 429 Retry-After responses, or use domain.verified webhooks when available.

faq.question: When can I create an inbox?
faq.answer: Create an inbox after the domain is verified and mail.receiving is true. Domain verification alone does not establish receiving readiness.

faq.question: What happens when I remove a domain?
faq.answer: The documented deletion restores the previous catch-all and removes only Cooper-created DNS records. User confirmation is required before removal.
